case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. T. L.
key_cases.holding: The court held that a parent may raise an unpreserved inadequate-assistance-of-counsel claim on direct appeal from a permanency judgment changing the plan from reunification to guardianship or APPLA, and remanded for an evidentiary record.
key_cases.relevance: Applies specifically to judgments moving the permanent plan to guardianship or another planned permanent living arrangement.
key_cases.quote: counsel appointed pursuant to ORS 419B.205 must be adequate, with adequacy determined using a standard of fundamental fairness

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. S. J. M.
key_cases.holding: Once DHS proves the ORS 419B.476 requirements for changing a permanency plan away from reunification, the burden shifts to the party invoking the ORS 419B.498(2) escape clause to prove a 'compelling reason' not to file a termination petition.
key_cases.relevance: Frames when an alternative permanent plan, rather than adoption, is 'better suited' to the child's health and safety needs.
key_cases.quote: it was parents' burden, as the parties seeking to invoke the escape clause, to show that there was a "compelling reason" under ORS 419B.498(2)

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. T. M. D.
key_cases.holding: The court held there is no statutory presumption or preference favoring termination over permanent guardianship, that the department bears the full burden on best interests, and on this record termination was not in the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that permanent guardianship is a legitimate competing permanency option that the court must weigh against termination on the evidence presented.
key_cases.quote: The department must prove only that that the parent's conduct justifies termination and that the best interest of the child will be served by termination.

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. J. G.
key_cases.holding: The court held that ICWA § 1914 permits an unpreserved 'active efforts' claim to be raised for the first time on appeal, but that ICWA did not require an active-efforts finding in a durable guardianship judgment, and affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Directly governs ICWA findings required for an Oregon durable guardianship under ORS 419B.366.
key_cases.quote: the juvenile court was not required under ICWA to make an "active efforts" finding in the guardianship judgment

key_cases.case_name: Dept. of Human Services v. R. F.
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of former foster parents' ORS 419B.116 motion to intervene in an ICWA case, holding the juvenile court was not compelled to find that existing parties could not adequately present the placement question, while noting intervention might later be required.
key_cases.relevance: Determines who has party status to contest the placement that will become the child's permanent home.
key_cases.quote: Accordingly, the Fs have not demonstrated that the juvenile court committed reversible error when it denied the motion to intervene.
